title: Monument class action alleges telehealth platform shared personal health info with third parties
summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Monument Inc., an online alcohol counseling and treatment company, alleging it shared patients' private health and identifiable information with third parties like Meta and Google without consent. The lawsuit claims Monument used a tracking pixel to transmit data including names, birthdates, and IP addresses, and that the company acknowledged disclosing information of over 108,000 individuals. The plaintiff seeks to represent a nationwide class and a Florida subclass, demanding a jury trial, injunctive relief, and damages.

title: Survey Signals Pause-and-Pivot Year for CEOs
summary: The 2023 Gartner CEO and Senior Business Executive Survey indicates a shift from short-term reactivity to cautious long-term planning, with CEOs focusing on business productivity and new three- to seven-year growth strategies. While growth remains a top priority, profitability is investors' primary concern, leading to an emphasis on multiyear productivity engineering and the creative application of new technologies like AI and automation. Talent and workforce issues, including shortages and compensation demands, continue to be significant challenges for executives.

title: Nextdoor Is Integrating Generative AI to Drive Engaging and Kind Conversations in the Neighborhood
summary: Nextdoor announced the integration of generative AI technologies, developed with OpenAI and leveraging the ChatGPT API, to foster more positive and engaging community interactions in the U.S. These new features will assist neighbors in writing posts that drive positive engagement and will suggest kinder revisions for potentially unkind comments. Nextdoor aims to personalize content and strengthen communities through these AI applications, led by Head of AI Qi He.

title: 5 Amazing Ways Meta (Facebook) Is Using Generative AI
summary: Meta, the parent company of Facebook, is heavily investing in generative AI despite its initial focus on the metaverse. The company is implementing generative AI across various platforms to enhance advertising, power AI-driven chat functionalities, revolutionize image and natural language generation, and ultimately, simplify content creation within its metaverse platform, Horizons. These initiatives aim to make content creation more accessible and potentially increase user engagement with Meta's virtual world.

title: Msci Kld 400 Social Index: Meaning, Example, FAQs
summary: The MSCI KLD 400 Social Index is a market capitalization-weighted stock index that focuses on large, mid, and small-cap U.S. companies with high environmental, social, and governance (ESG) standards, excluding certain industries. Founded as the Domini 400 Social Index, it was a pioneer in socially responsible investing. The index is reviewed quarterly and tends to be dominated by large American technology companies like Microsoft, NVIDIA, Alphabet, Tesla, and Visa.

title: CII Opposes Admitting Dual-Class Stock to S&P Indexes
summary: The Council of Institutional Investors (CII) has expressed "surprise and disappointment" over S&P Dow Jones Indices' decision to reverse its 2017 ban on admitting new dual-class stock companies to its indexes. This policy change, which allows companies like Blackstone into the S&P 500 despite having unequal voting rights, is criticized by CII for its opaque rationale and lack of investor consultation. S&P defends the change by citing the proliferation of dual-class structures, especially in tech, and the inconsistency of its previous grandfathering policy.

title: Is the Market Reacting Too Negatively to Pinterest Earnings?
summary: Pinterest's stock tumbled 25% despite beating Q1 2023 top and bottom-line estimates and growing monthly active users (MAUs). The sell-off was primarily driven by concerns over slowing growth, rising operating expenses (opex), and a GAAP net loss of $209 million due to restructuring charges. While analysts remain cautiously optimistic with reiterations, several lowered price targets, reflecting market uncertainty regarding the company's profitability amidst its strategic restructuring efforts.

title: Google’s Quantum Computing Technology in 2024 Review
summary: This article reviews Google's quantum computing technology in 2024, tracing its journey from the Quantum AI Lab's launch in 2013 to its achievement of "quantum supremacy" in 2019. It details Google's core quantum technologies, offerings like QVM and Cirq, and its efforts in post-quantum cryptography. The piece also outlines Google's main competitors, funding sources, significant customers, and strategic partnerships, while acknowledging challenges such as the refined classical algorithms that have narrowed the 'quantum supremacy' gap.

title: WSJ News Exclusive | Wendy’s, Google Train Next-Generation Order Taker: an AI Chatbot
summary: Wendy's is partnering with Google to automate its drive-through service using an AI chatbot. This chatbot is powered by Google's natural-language software and has been trained to understand various menu items and ordering styles, including specific Wendy's terminology like 'JBC' and 'biggie bags'. The initiative positions Wendy's among companies adopting generative AI for business growth.

title: Google AI pioneer says he quit to speak freely about technology's 'dangers'
summary: Geoffrey Hinton, an artificial intelligence pioneer, resigned from Google to openly discuss the potential "dangers" of AI, which he now believes could become smarter than humans much sooner than initially anticipated. He expressed concerns about AI's ability to create convincing fake content, displace workers, and be misused by malicious actors, urging policymakers to regulate the technology. Hinton clarified that Google acted responsibly and his departure was not to criticize his former employer.

title: Near Columbus, Wendy's tests an AI-powered chatbot for drive-thru orders
summary: Wendy's is piloting an AI-powered chatbot near Columbus to take drive-thru orders, aiming to improve customer service and address labor shortages. The system, developed with Google Cloud's AI software, is designed to understand natural speech and improve order accuracy, a key focus for the company. This move reflects a broader trend among fast-food chains to integrate AI and automation for enhanced efficiency and customer satisfaction.

title: Barry Diller joins News Corp and Axel Springer to fight ‘destructive’ AI
summary: Billionaire Barry Diller, chairman of IAC and Expedia, is collaborating with News Corp and Axel Springer to combat the perceived threat of generative AI to news publishers. Diller warns that AI, particularly platforms like ChatGPT, poses a "destructive" risk similar to the early internet's impact on journalism, advocating for redefined copyright laws and direct compensation for publishers whose content is used to train AI models. He also commented on Rupert Murdoch's legacy, stating the Dominion case stained his reputation.

Xperi aims to expand this into a global business, emphasizing an independent, unbiased media platform in the competitive smart TV market.

The piece argues that while Google has the potential to create a superior AI, Bard still requires significant development to live up to expectations.

The move signifies a major shift in local market measurement, leveraging Comscore's near census-level data and 48-hour post air-date reporting.

title: What you need to know about Temu, the online shopping app dominating download charts
summary: Online shopping app Temu, owned by Chinese company PDD Holdings Inc., has quickly risen to popularity in Canada with its aggressive marketing, low prices, and gamified shopping experience. While it offers bargain deals, experts caution consumers about product quality, potential environmental impact from shipping and returns, and data privacy concerns given its sister app's issues. The platform's "growth-at-all-costs" approach and referral schemes are disrupting the e-commerce market, leading to a "race to the bottom" that could hurt local businesses.

title: University of Chicago Gets Quantum Tech Funding From IBM, Google
summary: The University of Chicago has secured up to $150 million in funding from IBM and Google to accelerate the development of quantum computing. IBM plans to collaborate with the university and the University of Tokyo over ten years to build a quantum-centric supercomputer, a project valued at $100 million. This partnership aims to advance the field of quantum technology, which promises faster computing and enhanced online security.

title: Google announces US-Taiwan-Philippines cable with Chunghwa, Globe, and AT&T
summary: Google has announced plans for a new subsea cable system, TPU (Taiwan-Philippines-US), linking the US, Taiwan, and the Philippines, partnering with Chunghwa Telecom, Innove (Globe Group), and AT&T. This new cable, expected to be ready for service in 2025 with NEC as the supplier, will provide 260Tbps of capacity and offer an alternative route to Google's existing Apricot cable, enhancing resilience and capacity in the APAC region. Additionally, the article notes another subsea cable development, the EMC West system in the Middle East, being built by Center3 and ASN.

title: NVIDIA Announces DGX GH200 AI Supercomputer
summary: NVIDIA has unveiled the DGX GH200 AI supercomputer, designed to handle massive models for generative AI, recommender systems, and data analytics. This new system connects 256 Grace Hopper Superchips to function as a single 1-exaflop, 144TB GPU, offering significantly more memory than its predecessor. Companies like Google Cloud, Meta, and Microsoft are among the first to explore its capabilities, and NVIDIA is also building its own Helios supercomputer based on this design.

title: Google Pay
summary: This article from Barclays Private Bank details how to use Google Pay with Barclays debit cards, highlighting its security, convenience, and functionality for in-store and online payments. It provides step-by-step instructions for adding cards, answers frequently asked questions about eligibility, device compatibility, transaction limits, and what to do if a device is lost or stolen. Contact information for various client types is also included for support.

title: U.S. Supreme Court declines to hear bid to sue Reddit over child porn
summary: The U.S. Supreme Court has declined to hear a lawsuit attempting to hold Reddit Inc. liable for child pornography posted on its platform, upholding a lower court's decision that Reddit is shielded by Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act. The case explored the scope of a 2018 amendment, the Fight Online Sex Trafficking Act (FOSTA), which allows lawsuits if the claim involves child sex trafficking, but the court found Reddit did not "knowingly benefit" from such activity. This decision follows a similar sidestepping of Section 230 immunity in a separate case involving Google and YouTube.

title: Everything you need to know about Salesforce’s Q1 2024 financial results
summary: Salesforce, Inc. reported increased first-quarter adjusted earnings in Q1 2024 ($1.69 per share) and revenue growth of 11% year-over-year to $8.25 billion. All key operating segments showed growth, driven by its generative AI ecosystem including Einstein GPT, Slack GPT, and Tableau GPT. CEO Marc Benioff highlighted the role of the Salesforce GPT Trust Layer in securing customer data and enhancing enterprise automation.

title: Google head of communications and advisor to CEO Sundar Pichai to exit
summary: Corey duBrowa, Google's head of communications and a key advisor to CEO Sundar Pichai, is leaving the company after five years. He will be taking on the role of chief executive officer at BCW Global, a public relations firm based in New York.

title: Baidu Creates $140 Million Fund to Back ChatGPT-Like Startups
summary: Baidu Inc. has launched a 1 billion yuan ($140 million) fund to support Chinese startups developing generative AI, similar to ChatGPT services. This initiative aims to incubate projects built on Baidu's Ernie AI model, with individual deployments potentially reaching 10 million yuan. Venture capitalists like IDG Capital will assist in evaluating pitches and providing seed funding to promising founders.

title: Apple Bets On The Emerging Markets Growth Story
summary: Apple is increasingly focusing on emerging markets, particularly India, to drive growth amidst a challenging global smartphone market. The company achieved marginal growth in iPhone sales despite overall industry decline, with India seeing significant retail and manufacturing expansion plans. While services and financial technology offer long-term opportunities, the emerging markets strategy is a key component of Apple's immediate growth narrative, alongside ongoing share repurchases and dividend increases.

title: Vimeo is tuning out its streaming TV apps
summary: Vimeo is discontinuing its dedicated streaming TV apps for Apple TV, Android TV, Amazon Fire TV, and Roku starting June 27th. Users can still watch Vimeo content on their TVs by casting from the Vimeo mobile app via Apple AirPlay 2 or Google Chromecast. This move aligns with Vimeo's strategic shift in recent years from a consumer-facing streaming destination to focusing on video-streaming services for businesses.

title: Microsoft Inks Deal With NVIDIA-Backed CoreWeave
summary: Microsoft has signed a deal with NVIDIA-backed cloud-computing startup CoreWeave, planning to invest billions to bolster its cloud computing infrastructure for AI operations. This partnership will provide Microsoft easier access to NVIDIA’s GPUs, which are crucial for AI-based applications like ChatGPT, and aims to give Microsoft a competitive edge against rivals like Alphabet Inc. and Amazon Web Services. CoreWeave’s access to over 45,000 GPUs and its status as an elite CSP in the NVIDIA Partner Network positions it as a key enabler for Microsoft's AI endeavors.

title: Introducing Apple Vision Pro: Apple’s first spatial computer
summary: Apple has unveiled Apple Vision Pro, its first spatial computer, which blends digital content with the physical world using a three-dimensional user interface controlled by eyes, hands, and voice. Running on the new visionOS, Vision Pro features an ultra-high-resolution display system, custom Apple silicon, and offers new ways to interact with apps, enjoy entertainment, relive memories, and connect via FaceTime. The device is designed with advanced materials, focuses on privacy, and will be available early next year starting at $3,499 (U.S.).

title: Rep. Zoe Lofgren weighs in on quantum plans
summary: Rep. Zoe Lofgren, ranking member of the House Science Committee, discussed her objectives for reauthorizing the National Quantum Initiative Act (NQIA). Her goals include incorporating NASA, increasing fundamental scientific investment, and focusing on commercialization, while emphasizing bipartisanship. Lofgren also commented on the funding of the CHIPS and Science Act and the feasibility of a new package given the current political climate.

title: Sonos Prevails Over Google in $32.5 Million Lawsuit Win
summary: A San Francisco federal jury has ordered Google to pay $32.5 million to Santa Barbara-based Sonos for infringing on one of its wireless audio device patents. This decision, made on May 26, is part of ongoing legal battles between the two companies, stemming from a 2020 lawsuit by Sonos alleging patent infringement by Google in its Home and Chromecast Audio products. While Sonos had initially sought up to $3 billion in damages, the final settlement was reduced to $32.5 million.

FortiFlex aims to address the evolving needs of highly distributed networks by allowing organizations to pay by usage and manage licenses more efficiently across various deployment types.

title: Accenture looks to power AI efforts with $3 billion investment
summary: Accenture announced a significant $3 billion investment over three years into its data and AI practice, aiming to double the number of employees working with AI to 80,000. This move highlights a broader industry trend of companies scaling up generative AI offerings, following similar initiatives by Microsoft, Alphabet, and Salesforce. The investment also comes after recent layoffs at Accenture and includes the launch of an "AI Navigator for Enterprise" tool to guide businesses in AI adoption.

summary: AMD has launched its new Instinct MI300X AI accelerator chip, designed to compete with Nvidia's GPUs in the generative AI market. The company also introduced its Infinity Architecture Platform, powered by eight MI300X chips, and its ROCm software ecosystem. Despite these announcements, AMD's stock fell due to a lack of major customer endorsements for the new chips and details on pricing.

summary: AMD unveiled new details about its MI300X artificial intelligence chip, designed to challenge Nvidia's market dominance, but did not announce any major customers for the product. Analysts noted that Nvidia's strong market position is reinforced by its software ecosystem, which AMD is attempting to counter with its Rocm platform.

title: Someone is posing as a fake security company to create malicious GitHub repositories
summary: An unidentified actor is creating malicious GitHub repositories under the guise of a fake security company, High Sierra Cyber Security, offering exploits for popular products but delivering malware. VulnCheck researchers, who uncovered this activity, warn that security researchers are valuable targets and advise caution when downloading code from GitHub, recommending vetting code thoroughly or running unknown exploits in isolated virtual machines.

title: Dropbox review: Still the best at syncing and sharing
summary: This PCWorld review reaffirms Dropbox's position as a top choice for fast, reliable file synchronization and sharing, despite its limited free storage and lack of intermediate subscription tiers. While it excels in its core functionality and offers business-oriented features, its pricing model lacks options between the free 2GB and the paid 2TB. The article highlights its strengths for collaborative file access and its backup capabilities.

title: The Next Big Things From SAP
summary: SAP recently unveiled significant innovations at its Sapphire event in Orlando, focusing on responsible AI integrated into business solutions, ledger-based accounting for carbon tracking (green ledger initiative), and industry-specific networks to enhance supply-chain resilience. These advancements aim to help customers transform their business models in the cloud, prioritize sustainability, and boost agility in an evolving future. SAP is also expanding partnerships, like with Google Cloud for open data, and committing to upskill two million people globally to meet the demand for SAP experts.

title: Congress Large Cap Growth ETF Holdings
summary: The Congress Large Cap Growth ETF (CAML), established on August 22, 2023, is an actively managed fund investing in large-cap companies for long-term capital growth. With $333.49 million in assets under management and 41 holdings, its top investments include NVIDIA, Apple, and Alphabet. The ETF focuses on companies anticipated to experience earnings growth.

title: Arm, the Chip Designer, Files for an I.P.O. Expected to Be Among the Largest (Published 2023)
summary: Arm, the chip design company owned by SoftBank, has filed for an initial public offering (IPO) on the Nasdaq exchange, which is anticipated to be one of the largest in recent years. This move follows Nvidia's abandoned bid to acquire Arm for $40 billion 18 months prior. The IPO will provide SoftBank with additional capital for investments, and SoftBank will retain its position as Arm's controlling shareholder.

title: Will India be able to deal with Google’s adtech monopoly?
summary: This article examines Google's monopolization of the adtech sector, detailing how the company's acquisitions and anti-competitive practices have harmed media and newspaper publishers globally, including in India. It discusses actions taken by regulatory bodies in the EU, UK, and US, and suggests that India's current competition regime needs significant amendments to effectively address Google's dominant position and ensure fair market practices. The piece highlights the dire financial consequences for publishers and the need for greater transparency and regulation in the digital advertising landscape.

title: Invesco AI and Next Gen Software ETF
summary: This page provides a detailed profile of the Invesco AI and Next Gen Software ETF (IGPT), covering its price, performance, holdings, expenses, and ESG scores. The ETF focuses on technology equities, specifically software and artificial intelligence, with a significant concentration in large-cap U.S. technology companies. It also includes sections on historical trading data, fund flows, and comparisons to other technology equities ETFs.

title: Hedge fund exposure to 7 biggest tech stocks at record high, Goldman Sachs says
summary: Hedge funds have reached record exposure to the seven largest tech stocks by market capitalization, according to Goldman Sachs data, driven by strong performance and the artificial intelligence theme. These seven stocks, including Nvidia, Apple, and Microsoft, now constitute about 20% of the total net market value held by hedge funds tracked by Goldman Sachs. Despite the concentration risk, investment managers rationalize these allocations due to the significant returns generated by these companies this year.

title: Avis, Google, Hibbett, other settlement checks in the mail
summary: This article reports on several class action settlement checks being mailed to consumers from companies like Avis, Google, and Hibbett. These settlements address various issues including hidden e-toll fees, FACTA violations, illegal ATM fees, disposable contact lens price-fixing, data breaches, and privacy violations related to Google Photos. Readers have reported receiving payments ranging from tens to over a thousand dollars from these lawsuits.

title: Institute for National Defense and Security Research-Newsletter
summary: This article analyzes the impact of the Matsu undersea cable interruption on Taiwan's national defense and security, emphasizing the critical role of submarine cables for communication and military operations. It highlights how the CCP's grey zone tactics, including cable damage, undermine Taiwan's cyber resilience and calls for establishing comprehensive backup mechanisms, strengthening network infrastructure, and developing low-orbit satellites, drawing lessons from the Russo-Ukrainian War, to enhance Taiwan's communication system. The author stresses the need for integration between military and civilian technological capabilities and international cooperation to secure national communication.

title: Google Cloud, HCA team up to deploy AI in the emergency department
summary: HCA Healthcare is expanding its partnership with Google Cloud and Augmedix to deploy generative AI tools in emergency departments, aiming to improve documentation efficiency and allow clinicians more time for patient care. Following a successful pilot program in four hospitals, HCA is considering wider implementation of Google's generative AI, and also exploring the use of Google's medical large language model, Med-PaLM 2, for complex medical queries. The initiative focuses on enhancing workflows and caregiver support while acknowledging the need for careful ethical deployment and rigorous quality assessment of AI in healthcare.

title: Ginkgo Bioworks and Google Cloud Partner to Build Next Generation AI Platform for Biological Engineering and Biosecurity
summary: Ginkgo Bioworks and Google Cloud have announced a five-year strategic partnership to develop an AI platform for biological engineering and biosecurity. Ginkgo will leverage Google Cloud's Vertex AI and computational infrastructure to build new large language models across genomics, protein function, and synthetic biology, with Google Cloud providing funding and positioning Ginkgo as a key partner in developing foundation models for life sciences. This collaboration aims to accelerate innovation in areas like drug discovery, agriculture, manufacturing, and biosecurity, and will be discussed further at Google Cloud Next.

title: GM, Google exploring ways to use AI across automaker’s business
summary: General Motors and Google are expanding their partnership to explore the integration of AI technologies across GM's business operations. This collaboration builds on their previous work on GM's OnStar Interactive Virtual Assistant, aiming to revolutionize the automotive experience through generative AI. The companies anticipate AI will enhance vehicle validation, software, and in-car assistance, with potential future applications including customer interaction and new features.

title: SAP and Google Cloud Enhance Open Data Cloud With New Generative AI Solutions for Enterprises
summary: SAP and Google Cloud announced an expanded partnership to integrate generative AI solutions within their open data cloud. This collaboration will leverage SAP Datasphere and Google Cloud’s Vertex AI to create industry-specific solutions, starting with automotive, and enhance sustainability performance for enterprises. The partnership aims to provide customers with powerful new tools to improve business insights, analysis, and decision-making through responsible and secure AI deployment.

title: Invesco AI and Next Gen Software ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NYSEARCA:IGPT)
summary: The Invesco AI and Next Gen Software ETF (IGPT) invests in information technology equity, focusing on companies that derive over 50% of their revenue from the future media industry. As of April 2026, IGPT was trading at $71.12, showing a 19.6% increase year-to-date, with major holdings including Advanced Micro Devices, Alphabet, and NVIDIA. The ETF has current assets under management of $789.78 million and an aggregate rating of "Moderate Buy."

title: General Motors Teams Up with Google Cloud on AI Initiatives
summary: General Motors and Google Cloud are expanding their collaboration on AI initiatives, building on the success of GM's OnStar Interactive Virtual Assistant (IVA), which is powered by Google Cloud's conversational AI technologies. This partnership, which began in 2019 with Google built-in features in GM vehicles, now includes explorations into future generative AI deployments to enhance customer experience both inside and outside the vehicle. GM's innovative use of AI in its OnStar IVA has earned it a "Talent Transformation" award from Google Cloud, recognizing its successful and broad deployment of AI to handle over a million customer inquiries monthly.

title: HCA Healthcare collaborates with Google Cloud to bring generative AI to hospitals
summary: HCA Healthcare has partnered with Google Cloud to integrate generative AI into hospital workflows, aiming to improve efficiency in tasks like clinical documentation and patient handoffs. This collaboration builds on a 2021 strategic partnership and has already seen positive pilot results with emergency room physicians using AI for medical note-taking and nurses testing an AI-powered handoff report system. The initiative seeks to free up clinicians to focus more on patient care, leveraging technologies like Augmedix and exploring Google's Med-PaLM 2 LLM for complex medical queries, all while prioritizing patient privacy and data security.

title: How space traffic in orbit could spell trouble on Earth
summary: The increasing number of satellites in Earth's orbit, particularly large constellations like Starlink, significantly raises the risk of catastrophic collisions and the generation of more space debris. Such collisions could disrupt vital services on Earth, including GPS, communication, weather forecasting, and intelligence gathering. The current patchwork of international regulations is insufficient to manage this growing traffic, highlighting the urgent need for a formal, coordinated global system to prevent disasters and maintain the functionality of orbital infrastructure.

title: Leveraging Generative AI to Build Personalized Customer Journey Mapping
summary: This report details how marketing teams are utilizing Generative AI (GenAI) for customer personalization and workflow improvements. Based on a survey of 100 marketing professionals, it highlights GenAI's role in content creation, personalization, and the use of synthetic data, while also addressing its integration with existing marketing automation platforms. The findings indicate widespread adoption and positive impacts on efficiency, suggesting GenAI is a valuable, though not always central, tool for future customer journey mapping.

title: Get Ready for Google Cloud Firewall Plus, Network Integration Ease
summary: Palo Alto Networks and Google Cloud are introducing two new offerings to enhance cloud security: Cloud Firewall Plus and participation in the Google Cloud Network Service Integration Manager (NSIM). Cloud Firewall Plus provides a scalable, cloud-native firewall with Intrusion Prevention capabilities using Palo Alto Networks Threat Prevention technologies. The NSIM will simplify deployment and integration of VM-Series virtual Next-Generation Firewall (NGFWs), allowing for consistent security management across diverse environments.

title: Q&A: How to start learning natural language processing
summary: In this Q&A, Hobson Lane, co-author of "Natural Language Processing in Action," discusses how to begin learning NLP, including its benefits and challenges. He emphasizes the importance of curiosity and basic Python knowledge for beginners, and addresses common hurdles like OS compatibility and accessing high-quality labeled data. Lane also shares an optimistic outlook on NLP's potential for fostering cooperation and productive human thought, stressing that generative models are not the only, or always the best, approach to NLP.

title: Worker confidence in AI may be growing despite unease about the tech
summary: A Robert Half survey indicates growing worker confidence in generative AI, with 4 in 10 U.S. workers believing it will positively impact their careers, despite past unease regarding job displacement. The survey, conducted in May 2023, shows HR and tech professionals, along with younger generations, are particularly optimistic about AI's ability to automate tasks and increase efficiency. Companies are increasingly adopting AI for various functions, leading to a surge in demand for AI-related skills.

title: SAP nabs new global AI head from Microsoft, Walter Sun
summary: SAP has appointed Walter Sun, formerly VP of Copilot Applied Artificial Intelligence at Microsoft, as its new global head of AI. This strategic hire underscores SAP's commitment to prioritizing AI, following recent collaborations with Microsoft and Google Cloud to integrate generative AI into its enterprise offerings. Sun, with his extensive background in AI and machine learning, is tasked with leveraging SAP's broad applications and customer base to transform business operations through innovative AI solutions.

title: Bandwidth Partners with Google and Cognigy to Launch AIBridge, Integrating Artificial Intelligence with Contact Centers Using Maestro
summary: Bandwidth has announced a partnership with Google and Cognigy to launch AIBridge, a new capability within its Maestro platform. AIBridge enables enterprises to deploy voice-based AI tools to their contact centers, allowing for faster and more efficient call resolution in the communications cloud without direct agent intervention. This integration is designed to improve customer experience, increase agent satisfaction, and significantly reduce contact center operating costs by leveraging conversational AI from partners like Cognigy.AI and Google Cloud's Dialogflow.

title: Andretti special purpose acquisition company to merge with Boston-based AI startup
summary: The blank-check company started by former IndyCar driver Michael Andretti, Andretti Acquisition Corp., is merging with Boston-based artificial intelligence startup Zapata AI. This merger values Zapata at approximately $200 million, with the combined company's equity value projected to be between $281 million and $365 million depending on share redemptions. The transaction is anticipated to close in the first quarter of next year, bringing together Andretti's SPAC with a "generative AI software company" that has roots in quantum computing and focuses on industrial AI solutions.

title: Equinix Appoints Adam Berlew as Chief Marketing Officer
summary: Equinix, Inc. has announced the appointment of Adam Berlew as Chief Marketing Officer (CMO), effective immediately. Berlew brings over 25 years of experience in strategic marketing and global leadership, having previously served as a Vice President of Global Marketing at Equinix from 2012 to 2015. In his new role, he will be responsible for driving customer acquisition and revenue growth through marketing strategies aligned with Platform Equinix's vision.

title: Snapchat announces new features to protect teenagers from online risks
summary: Snapchat is introducing new features to enhance teen safety by implementing a strike system for inappropriate content and pop-up warnings when strangers attempt to contact them. These measures aim to prevent contact from unknown individuals and expose teens to only age-appropriate content, alongside educational resources for parents. The updates also include requirements for more mutual friends before teens can add new contacts.

title: Why Goldman Sachs believes that Spotify will remain the world’s dominant music streaming service in 2030
summary: Goldman Sachs predicts that Spotify will remain the dominant music streaming service globally through 2030, maintaining its market share around the mid-30% level outside of China. Despite facing competition from larger tech conglomerates and new services like TikTok Music, Spotify's market share outside of China has remained broadly stable since 2017. Goldman Sachs also anticipates YouTube Music will become the second-largest DSP by 2030, surpassing Apple Music, and foresees consolidation among smaller streaming platforms.

title: ALPS OShares Global Internet Giants ETF (OGIG) Stock Price, Holdings, Dividend Yield
summary: This article provides a detailed overview of the ALPS OShares Global Internet Giants ETF (OGIG), including its current stock price, key financial ratios like PE and PB, and dividend yield. It outlines the ETF's top holdings as of its latest N-PORT filing, such as Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta, and Palantir, and discusses the ETF's performance metrics and historical data. The report also highlights recent trading activities within the ETF, including new buys and stocks that have been reduced or sold out.

title: Breakthrough and Enovis (TM) Announce Official Partnership, Empowering Private Practice Healthcare to Help Improve Quality of Care While Increasing Profitability
summary: Breakthrough, a leader in conservative care marketing solutions, and Enovis™ Corporation, a pioneer in innovative rehabilitation technologies, have announced an official partnership. This collaboration aims to empower private practice healthcare providers to improve patient care quality and increase profitability by promoting innovative therapeutic technologies directly to patients through data-driven marketing campaigns. The partnership enables clinics to confidently adopt new technologies, like laser therapy, by offering solutions to overcome declining insurance reimbursements through cash-based services.

title: More writers sue OpenAI for copyright infringement over AI training
summary: A group of U.S. authors, including Pulitzer Prize winner Michael Chabon, has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI in federal court in San Francisco. They allege that OpenAI misused their copyrighted writings to train its AI-powered chatbot, ChatGPT, without permission. This is at least the third such class-action lawsuit by authors against OpenAI, with the plaintiffs seeking monetary damages and an injunction against OpenAI's business practices.

title: US, Vietnam firms talk business during Biden visit; AI and Boeing deals unveiled
summary: During U.S. President Joe Biden's visit to Hanoi, executives from top American and Vietnamese firms in technology, semiconductors, and aviation met to establish new business partnerships. The meeting led to significant deals, including Vietnam Airlines purchasing 50 Boeing 737 Max jets and plans for Microsoft and Nvidia to advance AI solutions and chip design centers in Vietnam. These collaborations aim to deepen cooperation in key technological sectors and reinforce Vietnam's role in global supply chains, especially in chipmaking.

title: OpenAI’s Sam Altman tells Salesforce’s Marc Benioff that AI ‘hallucinations’ are more feature than bug
summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman suggested to Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff that AI "hallucinations" should be seen as a feature, not a bug, emphasizing their creative potential. This discussion took place at the Dreamforce conference where Salesforce rolled out new AI products, integrating with platforms like Google Workspace. Altman's perspective highlights a focus on generative AI's creative capabilities over its strict adherence to factual accuracy.

title: Pulitzer winner Chabon, other authors sue Meta over AI program
summary: A group of writers, including Pulitzer Prize winner Michael Chabon, Tony-winning playwright David Henry Hwang, and authors Matthew Klam, Rachel Louise Snyder, and Ayelet Waldman, have sued Meta Platforms in San Francisco federal court. They accuse Meta of misusing their copyrighted works to train its Llama artificial-intelligence software, alleging that pirated versions of their writings were used in the training datasets. This lawsuit follows a similar proposed class-action suit against OpenAI by the same authors, highlighting a growing legal challenge for AI companies regarding intellectual property.

title: Infosys only Indian company in top 100 TIME World's Best Companies list
summary: Infosys is the sole Indian company to secure a spot in the top 100 of TIME Magazine and Statista's World's Best Companies of 2023 list, ranking 64th. The list evaluates companies based on revenue growth, employee satisfaction, and ESG data. While other Indian companies like Wipro, Mahindra Group, and Reliance Industries were present in the larger list of 750, Infosys stood out for its high growth rate and position among top professional services firms.

title: In Silico Part - IV : AI and its impact on labor, productivity, and tech-driven deflation
summary: This article examines the uncertain macroeconomic impacts of Artificial Intelligence, focusing on its potential effects on labor, productivity, and deflation. It discusses AI's role in creative destruction, its likelihood of augmenting rather than fully replacing human labor in the near term, and its historical and future contributions to productivity growth and deflationary pressures. The authors conclude that AI is anticipated to boost productivity and exert deflationary forces, while acknowledging that long-term labor displacement is possible, leading to the creation of new job categories.

title: Publishers’ Lawsuit Accuses Libgen of “Staggering” Copyright Infringement
summary: Major publishers including Cengage, Macmillan Learning, McGraw Hill, and Pearson Education have filed a copyright infringement lawsuit against Library Genesis (Libgen), a prominent "shadow library," in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York. The lawsuit claims "staggering" levels of infringement, with over six million files on Libgen infringing copyrights, and seeks damages, an injunction, and control over Libgen's domains. Publishers argue that Libgen's operations cause significant financial and creative harm, undermining the publishing industry and authors' income, despite the site's claim of providing free access to educational literature.

title: Manyika appointed to Airbnb board
summary: Google's Research, Technology and Society senior vice-president, James Manyika, a Zimbabwean-born businessman, has been appointed to the board of American online homestay firm, Airbnb Inc., effective immediately. Manyika, an expert in AI and technology's impact on society, will help Airbnb leverage artificial intelligence and joins eight other board members at the US$91.96 billion valued company. His extensive background includes roles at McKinsey & Company, advising the White House, and serving on various influential boards, bringing significant expertise in technology, economy, and global trends to Airbnb.

title: Morgan Stanley’s AI Assistant Marks New Era For Finance Sector
summary: Morgan Stanley has launched an internal AI assistant, 'AI @ Morgan Stanley Assistant', built on OpenAI's GPT-4 software. This move positions Morgan Stanley as a pioneer among major banks in utilizing generative AI for financial advisors and support staff. While the bank also faces a significant lawsuit, its stock saw a slight increase following the AI announcement, signaling a new era for AI in the finance sector.

title: Oracle says it's ready to cater to Canadian banks' open banking needs
summary: Oracle has declared its readiness to support Canadian banks with their open banking requirements, offering technology solutions as Canada implements its framework. Oracle's executive vice president for financial services, Sonny Singh, noted that the company's existing financial products, used globally, are well-positioned for this shift. This comes as Canadian banks are increasingly partnering with fintech firms and Oracle, despite recent market value losses due to strong cloud-computing competition.

title: Communications ETF XLC Offers Loud & Clear Exposure to the Space
summary: The Communication Services Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLC) provides investors with exposure to the growing digital side of the U.S. economy, encompassing communications, media, and technology companies. Launched following a 2018 GICS reclassification, XLC tracks a market-cap-weighted index of U.S. telecom, media, and entertainment components of the S&P 500, with top holdings including Meta Platforms and Alphabet. This ETF offers an accessible and low-cost way to invest in leading digital economy companies.

title: Google to Pay $93 Million for Tricking Users
summary: Google has agreed to pay $93 million to the state of California for violating consumer protection laws by deceptively tracking users' locations. The settlement stems from a multi-year investigation revealing that Google continued to collect location data for advertising even after users attempted to opt out. As part of the agreement, Google must increase transparency regarding its location tracking practices and provide users with more control and information about how their data is used.

title: 3 Quantum Computing Stocks That Should Be on Every Investor’s Radar This Fall
summary: This article highlights three leading quantum computing stocks: IBM, Alphabet, and Microsoft, emphasizing their significant advancements in the field. IBM is recognized for its quantum breakthrough with over 100 qubits. Alphabet's quantum computer can solve complex problems far faster than traditional supercomputers, while Microsoft is advancing quantum computing to revolutionize chemistry and materials science.

title: Expedia Group builds generative AI into multiple products in its “Fall Release”
summary: Expedia Group is unveiling its "Fall Release 2023," introducing numerous features and products for travelers and supplier partners, heavily integrating generative AI. Key updates include AI-powered conversational capabilities within its apps, dynamic travel guides, and "EG Labs" for consumer feedback on new tech. The release also brings influencer content, group trip planning tools, and AI-driven recommendations for hotel partners to enhance performance and guest insights.

title: Cisco Buys Cybersecurity Provider Splunk for $28 Billion
summary: Cisco Systems is acquiring cybersecurity software company Splunk for $28 billion ($157 per share in cash), a move seen by analysts as an "aggressive strategic play" in the cybersecurity market. This acquisition is expected to accelerate Cisco's revenue growth and gross margins, becoming cash flow positive in the first fiscal year. The deal, which provided a significant premium to Splunk shareholders, highlights Cisco's intent to compete strongly in the AI-driven software space against major rivals.

title: What Market Pros Saw Last Earnings Season That Spurred Investments in Tech and AI Stocks
summary: Market experts, managing over $67 billion, analyzed second-quarter earnings reports and concluded that the bull market has room to run, a U.S. recession is unlikely, consumer spending remains strong, and AI is not in a bubble but rather a significant driver of corporate profits. They identified key sectors and companies benefiting from current growth trends, including broad-market strength beyond AI and Big Tech, and a re-emerging strong momentum in European economies.

title: SK Telecom to triple investment in AI
summary: SK Telecom, Korea's largest mobile carrier, plans to triple its investment in AI, shifting its focus from its traditional telecommunications business. The company aims for 33% of its total investment over the next five years to go into AI, targeting 25 trillion won ($18.5 billion) in annual revenue by 2028. Its AI strategy centers on its Korean large language model A dot, urban air mobility (UAM), and AI health care solutions.

title: The fraud of the Writers Guild contract: Reject and mobilize against this rotten deal!
summary: This article criticizes the tentative agreement reached by the Writers Guild of America (WGA) with studios, networks, and streaming services, urging writers to reject it as a "fraud." The author argues the WGA leadership does not represent its members' interests, highlighting issues like the isolation of the strike, the anti-democratic process of ending the strike before ratification, and the perceived inadequacies of the contract regarding residuals and AI. The article claims the deal benefits corporations and will not prevent job losses or the decline in writers' incomes, calling for writers to mobilize through rank-and-file committees for a more radical struggle.

title: What Is a CTA and Why It Matters In Marketing (Plus Cool CTA Examples)
summary: This article explains what a Call-to-Action (CTA) is and why it's crucial for digital marketing conversions. It highlights how strong CTAs transform visitors into customers, providing statistics on their effectiveness and offering best practices for creating and optimizing them, including clarity, urgency, and personalization. The article also covers how to measure CTA performance using metrics like Click-Through Rate, Cost Per Click, and Conversion Rate, and provides examples from Spotify, CrazyEgg, and ClickUp.

title: 10 Best Live TV Streaming Services for Cord Cutters in 2023
summary: This article lists the 10 best live TV streaming services for cord-cutters in 2023, based primarily on subscriber numbers. It details the evolving landscape of television consumption, from traditional cable to streaming, highlighting the recent challenges faced by live TV streaming services and YouTube TV's growth due to its NFL Sunday Ticket acquisition. The piece provides an overview of each of the top 10 services, including their features, pricing, and channel lineups.

title: Palantir: Implications Of The $28B Mega Cisco-Splunk Deal (NYSE:PLTR)
summary: Cisco's $28 billion acquisition of Splunk underscores the increasing value of AI capabilities in the industry, raising questions about potential takeover targets. Palantir Technologies, with its aggressive focus on AI and growth in Business Intelligence, is identified as a possible acquisition candidate. This deal highlights the broader trend of large corporations seeking to acquire advanced AI capabilities for long-term revenue growth.

title: Okta Introduces Okta AI – Securely Connecting People to Technology in the AI Era
summary: Okta, Inc. has announced Okta AI, a new suite of AI-powered capabilities designed to enhance security, user experience, and app development within its Workforce Identity Cloud and Customer Identity Cloud. This initiative leverages Okta's unique threat intelligence and Identity data, in collaboration with Google Cloud's Vertex AI, to accelerate AI innovation for Identity. Okta AI aims to provide real-time Identity actions while maintaining strict privacy and compliance standards for customer data.

title: PayPal Makes Good on Its Apple Pay Card Vow
summary: PayPal has fulfilled its promise to integrate its PayPal and Venmo credit and debit cards with Apple Wallet, nearly a year after the initial vow. This integration allows users to add their cards to Apple Pay for in-app and Safari browser transactions. Former CEO Dan Schulman stated that this move aims to offer more choice to PayPal's merchants and increase branded transactions, citing a similar success with Google Pay in Germany.

title: This bond market is providing double-digit returns
summary: Catastrophe bonds, or "cat bonds," are offering investors double-digit returns, with some seeing as high as 16% this year, despite broader bond market turmoil. These bonds protect insurers and companies from large disaster losses, paying investors attractive coupons if no such events occur. The market dynamically adjusts to rising interest rates and increased risk premiums due to climate change, attracting more asset managers and issuers while requiring investors to accept a unique risk profile.

title: Who owns the news? Mail titles, News UK and Reach dominate, report finds
summary: A new report, "Who Owns the UK Media? 2023," reveals that three companies—DMG Media, News UK, and Reach—control 90% of the UK's national newspaper market and over 40% of the top 50 online news brands. This concentration, also prevalent in local news, raises concerns about media diversity and the influence these conglomerates exert on the national agenda. The report calls for urgent reform to address this concentrated ownership and regulate the dominant tech platforms that act as gatekeepers to news.

title: PacBio Announces Complete Computational Workflow for Human Whole Genome Sequencing Data Analysis
summary: PacBio has announced the availability of its WGS Variant Pipeline, a complete and standardized computational method for analyzing HiFi whole genome sequencing (WGS) data. This new software integrates PacBio and third-party tools into a single workflow, allowing customers to detect various variant types, along with methylation and phasing data, more efficiently than before. The pipeline aims to streamline data analysis, enable deeper biological discovery, and is accessible through several bioinformatics analysis platforms.

title: Generative AI Delivers a Boost to Cloud Computing
summary: Cloud computing companies are experiencing a rebound after a difficult period, driven by improving fundamentals and the increasing importance of generative AI. Spending on cloud computing is projected to rise by nearly 22% in 2023, and cloud providers are capitalizing on this trend by integrating AI-incorporated solutions and monetizing AI-as-a-service. This surge in AI adoption is expected to lead to better-than-expected revenue and profit growth for companies in the cloud computing sector.

title: Citi Maintains Alphabet-A(GOOGL.US) With Buy Rating, Maintains Target Price $280
summary: Citi analyst Ronald Josey has maintained a Buy rating on Alphabet-A (GOOGL.US) and kept the target price at $280. According to TipRanks, the analyst boasts a 60.5% success rate and an average return of 24.6% over the past year. The information is provided for informational purposes and is not investment advice.

title: Google joins Adobe, Microsoft in promising to protect its AI users from copyright claims
summary: Google has announced it will legally protect users of its generative AI products against copyright infringement claims. This move follows similar commitments from other tech giants like Adobe and Microsoft, aiming to alleviate concerns about intellectual property violations in AI-generated content. The commitment means Google will shoulder legal responsibility for its users in such cases.

title: Malicious “RedAlert - Rocket Alerts” application targets Israeli phone calls, SMS, and user information
summary: Cloudflare's Cloudforce One Threat Operations Team discovered a malicious Android application impersonating the legitimate "RedAlert - Rocket Alerts" app, widely used in Israel for airstrike alerts. This malicious version, distributed via a deceptive website, collects sensitive user data including call logs, SMS, contacts, and account information, while mimicking the original app's functionality. Users who installed the Android version from `redalerts[.]me` are advised to delete it immediately and reinstall the authentic app from the Google Play Store.

title: Gartner Identifies the Top 10 Strategic Technology Trends for 2024
summary: Gartner has announced its top 10 strategic technology trends for 2024, emphasizing the need for organizations to act boldly amidst technological disruptions and socioeconomic uncertainties. The trends, presented at Gartner IT Symposium/Xpo 2023, highlight the increasing role of AI, sustainability, and intelligent automation in driving business value and resilience. Key themes include the democratization of Generative AI, AI Trust, Risk and Security Management, AI-Augmented Development, and the emergence of Machine Customers and Industry Cloud Platforms.

title: Will AI Take Your Job? Answer: Yes, No & Awesomely So
summary: This article explores the impact of AI on jobs, arguing against the doomsday predictions of massive layoffs. While acknowledging that job displacement will occur, the author, Satyen K. Bordoloi, emphasizes that AI will also create new opportunities and redefine the job market, leading to increased productivity and a higher standard of living in the long run. The piece encourages individuals to adapt and leverage AI for personal and professional growth, viewing it as an opportunity rather than a threat.

title: DaVita Collaborates with Google Cloud to Develop Customized Clinical Operating System Designed to Transform Kidney Care
summary: DaVita Inc. and Google Cloud have partnered to develop a new clinical operating system called Center Without Walls (CWOW) to transform kidney care for over 200,000 DaVita patients. This system centralizes clinical documentation and leverages AI and analytics from over 30 million dialysis treatments annually to improve clinical outcomes and streamline workflows. Built on Google Cloud's infrastructure, CWOW aims to enhance data sharing between care teams, physician partners, and hospitals, ultimately improving patient quality of life and lowering care costs.

title: Stanford’s AI transparency index shows foundational models are shrouded in secrecy
summary: A Stanford University report reveals that most popular foundational AI models from companies like OpenAI, Google, and Meta lack transparency regarding their development and societal impact. Meta's Llama 2 topped the transparency index, while OpenAI's GPT-4 scored lower despite extensive public information from partners, indicating that open-source models generally lead in transparency. The researchers highlight the need for greater disclosure to inform policymakers and foster trust in AI, especially as regulations like the EU's Artificial Intelligence Act emerge.

title: Google Pay Enters Lending Business In India
summary: Google Pay is expanding its services in India by entering the lending business, partnering with regulated lenders to offer various credit initiatives. This move includes providing personal loans, merchant financing, and sachet loans, leveraging the UPI network and Rupay credit cards. The Reserve Bank of India is closely monitoring the rapid growth in unsecured loans, advising banks and NBFCs to strengthen their risk management and underwriting standards.

title: Ask AI Guru: Genpact turns to generative AI to help employees learn
summary: Genpact, a NYSE-listed professional services company, has rolled out an internal generative AI chatbot called "AI Guru" to enhance employee learning and development. This tool, powered by Microsoft Azure OpenAI Service, helps employees with tasks such as IT migration, test case generation, and management advice, and provides 24/7 access to collective expertise from internal "master gurus." title: T. Rowe Price Capital Appreciation Equity ETF (TCAF): A Promising Active Fund
summary: The T. Rowe Price Capital Appreciation Equity ETF (TCAF) has shown significant growth since its launch in June 2023, accumulating over $600 million in assets. TCAF's investment philosophy emphasizes strong performance in areas like technology, healthcare, and consumer discretionary.

title: Cathie Wood Goes Big Into ProShares Bitcoin, Dumps Grayscale
summary: Cathie Wood's ARK Next Generation Internet ETF has significantly altered its Bitcoin-related holdings by selling all 2.25 million shares of the Grayscale Bitcoin Trust and purchasing 4.32 million shares of the ProShares Bitcoin Strategy ETF. This move was made "out of an abundance of caution" regarding the Grayscale fund's conversion to a spot-Bitcoin ETF and reflects Wood's continued optimism about Bitcoin. The ARK ETF also bought shares of the ARK 21Shares Active Bitcoin Futures Strategy ETF and sold Coinbase Global Inc. shares.

title: Capital One Job Cuts Signal Trouble for IT Labor Market
summary: Capital One Financial Corp. has cut 1,100 positions within its technology department, specifically impacting its "agile" group. This move signals a potential spread of tech sector layoffs into corporate IT departments, which had previously been largely insulated. The job cuts reflect companies' belt-tightening measures amidst fears of a recession.

title: Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff says San Francisco cleaned up its troubled downtown after he pressured City Hall
summary: Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff stated that San Francisco officials cleaned up the city's downtown in response to his pressure, ahead of the company's annual Dreamforce conference. Benioff had previously warned that the conference might leave the city due to concerns about homelessness and drug use. While happy with the short-term improvements, Benioff emphasized that more work is needed to address ongoing issues like homelessness and public safety for Dreamforce to consistently remain in San Francisco.

title: Inflection AI Announces $1.3 Billion of Funding Led by Current Investors, Microsoft, and NVIDIA
summary: Inflection AI announced a $1.3 billion funding round led by Microsoft, Reid Hoffman, Bill Gates, Eric Schmidt, and NVIDIA, bringing its total raised to $1.525 billion. The funding will support the company's work on Pi, a personal AI designed for natural text and voice conversations. Inflection AI is also building the world's largest AI cluster with 22,000 NVIDIA H100 Tensor Core GPUs in partnership with CoreWeave and NVIDIA.

title: Big Tech Expects Some Assets to Last Longer. But the Boost to Profit Is Temporary.
summary: A growing number of tech companies, including Alphabet, IBM, and Akamai Technologies, are extending the estimated working lives of their servers and network equipment. This accounting change reflects a slower pace of chip development and temporarily boosts profits by cutting costs at a challenging time for the industry. Other major tech firms like Meta Platforms, Microsoft, Oracle, and Amazon.com have also revised these estimates since 2022.

title: Qualcomm, Iridium Take Aim at Satellite-to-Mobile Phone Market
summary: Qualcomm and Iridium Communications are collaborating to introduce technology enabling satellite messaging for smartphone users in areas without cellular service. This partnership will initially offer a satellite-based emergency service for Android devices equipped with Qualcomm's premium chips. The move aims to bring satellite connectivity to a broader market, similar to the feature available on newer iPhones.

title: Sophia Velastegui
summary: Sophia Velastegui is Senior Vice President and Chief Product Officer of Aptiv, an automotive and autonomous tech company, where she drives innovation and growth. summary: DocuSign announced a new round of layoffs, affecting 10% of its staff, or approximately 700 employees, primarily in its field organization. This decision follows a 9% staff reduction in September and aims to position the company for profitable growth and free up resources for investments. These layoffs are part of a broader trend of continued job cuts across the tech industry, with other major companies like Google, Meta, and Amazon also announcing reductions.

summary: Alphabet's 20-for-1 stock split, following similar moves by Apple and Tesla, is unlikely to fundamentally change the company's valuation but aims to make shares more accessible to smaller investors and potentially gain entry into the Dow Jones Industrial Average. summary: A Gartner Peer Community report from August 2023 surveyed 125 IT leaders on their organizations' Generative AI (GenAI) planning for 2024. A significant majority expect their GenAI strategy to change and anticipate increased spending in 2024, often relying on vendors for implementation, particularly in customer service, resource automation, and software development.

summary: Cloud services provider Sada Systems Inc. has been acquired by Insight Enterprises Inc. for $410 million. title: Mindlessly scroll on bike? ‘Tiktok fitness powered by Peloton’, stock soars
summary: Peloton has announced a partnership with TikTok to create a new fitness hub called #TikTokFitness, powered by Peloton. This collaboration aims to bring short-form fitness videos, live classes, instructor series, and celebrity collaborations to TikTok's vast audience. summary: Qualcomm (QCOM) recently unveiled its new Snapdragon XR2+ Gen 2 Platform chip for virtual and augmented reality (VR/AR). This development could intensify competition in the growing VR headset market, especially following Apple's Vision Pro and Meta's dominance in 2023.

summary: The E.W. Scripps Company, in partnership with Google, has announced its second class of 13 veteran print journalists for the Journalism Journey Initiative. This expansion follows a successful first year and builds on Google's multiyear financial commitment to the initiative.

summary: Isomorphic Labs, an AI spin-off of Alphabet's DeepMind, has secured partnerships with Eli Lilly And Co and Novartis AG, totaling approximately $3 billion. summary: NVIDIA announced at CES that Li Auto has selected NVIDIA DRIVE Thor for its next-generation EVs, while GWM, ZEEKR, and Xiaomi have adopted the NVIDIA DRIVE Orin platform. summary: Pinterest is positioned as a leading social commerce platform for 2024 due to its "frictionless soft sales" approach, attracting 482 million global monthly active users. Analysts are largely bullish on Pinterest, with several firms upgrading their ratings and issuing positive price targets.

summary: Applied Materials announced a collaboration with Google to advance next-generation augmented reality (AR) computing platforms. This partnership aims to combine Applied Materials' expertise in materials engineering with Google's platforms, products, and services to develop lightweight visual display systems for AR experiences. The companies plan to accelerate the development of future AR products, applications, and services.

summary: This article explores how generative AI can transform HR systems from basic record keepers into intelligent agents, enhancing self-service, automation, and user experience. summary: Fortinet has partnered with Google Cloud to expand its SASE Points-of-Presence (POPs) to new locations, enhancing its Universal SASE solution's global reach. This collaboration aims to provide secure access to applications for hybrid workforces, leveraging Google Cloud's infrastructure for improved performance and cost efficiency. The expanded partnership will accelerate customer adoption of Fortinet's integrated cloud-delivered security.

title: 12 Lessons the Market Taught Investors in 2023
summary: The article outlines 12 crucial investment lessons from 2023, emphasizing that market forecasts are often inaccurate and valuations cannot be used for market timing. summary: The article discusses how the 60/40 portfolio, despite predictions of its demise after a challenging 2022, rebounded significantly in 2023 with an 18% return. The piece also delves into the future prospects and potential challenges for the 60/40 portfolio, including inflation and moderate equity returns, while emphasizing its long-term resilience.

summary: SKYX Platforms Corp. debuted its patented All-in-One Smart Platform at CES 2024, aiming to make existing homes technologically advanced. This platform integrates multiple smart home features like a smoke/CO detector, smart speaker, Wi-Fi repeater, and various lighting controls, all controllable via app and voice commands. The product installs easily into a ceiling and supports major smart home ecosystems, with SKYX also renewing a global licensing agreement with GE.

summary: REX Shares, in collaboration with Tuttle Capital Management, has expanded its T-REX Single-Stock ETF suite by adding three new products: 2X Long Apple Daily Target ETF (AAPX), 2X Long Alphabet Daily Target ETF (GOOX), and 2X Long Microsoft Daily Target ETF (MSFX). summary: REX Shares and Tuttle Capital Management have expanded their T-REX Single-Stock ETF suite by introducing new offerings for Apple (CBOE: AAPX), Alphabet (CBOE: GOOX), and Microsoft (CBOE: MSFX). summary: Telesat has partnered with Aalyria to deploy its Spacetime next-generation networking software for the Telesat Lightspeed Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellation. Spacetime leverages machine learning and AI to optimize network orchestration, ensuring efficient data flow and high-quality service by analyzing millions of paths and dynamically routing traffic. This technology, proven through its use at Google and Alphabet, will also enable the constellation to learn and make faster, more efficient decisions over time.

summary: During CES 2024, numerous device manufacturers unveiled new OLED-powered products across TVs, monitors, and laptops. Additionally, several companies showcased advanced OLED and MicroLED prototypes, highlighting future display technologies.

summary: Victoria's Secret & Co (VS&Co) has partnered with Google Cloud to integrate AI and generative AI technologies, aiming to enhance personalized online shopping experiences and improve operational efficiencies. The collaboration includes developing a generative-AI powered conversational assistant for product recommendations and optimizing supply chain and human resources. This initiative builds on VS&Co's existing AI-powered product search and underscores the growing importance of AI in the fashion industry for customer service and operational advancements.

summary: Victoria's Secret & Co. (VS&Co) has partnered with Google Cloud to integrate AI and generative AI technologies, aiming to create more personalized online shopping experiences and improve operational efficiencies. The collaboration will leverage Vertex AI for a conversational assistant offering tailored product recommendations and enhance search capabilities on their website and mobile app. This initiative builds on VS&Co's acquisition of Adore Me, which already uses Google Cloud's AI, and seeks to optimize internal operations, marketing, supply chain, and HR.

summary: Wells Fargo's virtual assistant app, Fargo, powered by Google's AI, has handled 20 million interactions since its March launch and is projected to reach 100 million annually. The bank is aggressively deploying generative AI, including applications for back-office efficiency and a new Livesync app for financial planning. Wells Fargo emphasizes a multi-LLM, multi-cloud strategy on its "Tachyon" platform, and views multimodal LLMs and "agentic" AI as future critical developments, while navigating regulatory challenges.

title: Lawyers for Google app developers get $26 mln in antitrust settlement
summary: A U.S. federal judge approved a $26 million payout to lawyers representing Android software developers in an antitrust settlement with Google. This payout is part of a larger $112 million settlement, which includes $90 million in cash for developers and $22 million in savings from Google agreeing to maintain a reduced 15% service fee until May 2025 for developers' first $1 million in annual revenue. The ruling comes amidst other antitrust challenges against Google, including a recent jury verdict loss to Epic Games and a $700 million settlement with states and consumers.

title: Meta to default teen Facebook, Instagram users to most restrictive settings
summary: Meta Platforms announced it will set the default content settings for teenage users on Facebook and Instagram to the most restrictive to enhance their safety. This decision follows a lawsuit by 42 attorneys general alleging harm to teenage users by social media platforms. The update will hide more sensitive content, such as discussions of self-harm and eating disorders, and apply to both new and existing teen users.

title: How Stantec and WSP became Canada’s unlikely stock market stars — and made engineering sexy
summary: Stantec and WSP Global, two Canadian engineering firms, have become unexpected stock market stars with their shares soaring 242% and 197% respectively over five years, outperforming even major U.S. tech companies. Their success is attributed to shifting focus from fixed-price construction contracts to per-hour consulting fees, diversifying through acquisitions, expanding into areas like water infrastructure, and disciplined growth strategies focused on profitability rather than just revenue. Both companies prioritize strategic acquisitions, debt management, and maximizing workforce utilization, making engineering an attractive investment sector.

title: Monday.com review: Work management platform works best when you pay for it
summary: This review offers an in-depth look at Monday.com, a versatile "Work OS" designed for project management, process monitoring, and team collaboration. While it excels in power, flexibility, and ease of use, the review highlights that its full potential and most compelling features are unlocked in its paid tiers. The analysis covers pricing, core features like intelligent tables and integrations, low-code programming capabilities, and its workflow advantages compared to rivals, ultimately recommending the Standard tier for its value.

title: NetApp Hires AWS Executive To Manage Global Cloud Sales
summary: NetApp has hired Ashish Dhawan, formerly AWS's managing director and worldwide head of enterprise workload sales, as its new senior vice president of global cloud sales. This new role aims to strengthen NetApp's commitment to cloud sales and strategy, with Dhawan responsible for developing and executing the company's cloud sales strategy across all major cloud providers. This is NetApp's second high-profile hire this year, following Riccardo Di Blasio as SVP of North America sales.

summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman expressed his motivation to further invest in nuclear fusion, emphasizing that a breakthrough in energy is crucial to meet the immense future demands of artificial intelligence. He believes that without significant advancements in clean energy, the growing energy needs of AI cannot be sustainably met.

summary: AST SpaceMobile has secured a strategic investment of up to $206.5 million from AT&T, Google, and Vodafone. With significant growth projected in key markets and a strong track record of project execution, AES aims to capitalize on the increasing demand for clean energy in the tech industry.

summary: Retail companies Wayfair and Macy's have announced significant job cuts as layoffs deepen across the sector. summary: Online retailer eBay is cutting approximately 1,000 jobs, or 9% of its full-time workforce, citing that its employee count and costs have outpaced its business growth in a slowing economy. This move follows a trend of layoffs across the tech industry, where companies that rapidly expanded during the COVID-19 pandemic are now trimming expenses. summary: eBay announced plans to cut 9% of its workforce, or 1,000 jobs, which led to a nearly 3% surge in its stock price. summary: Salesforce Inc. is reportedly laying off approximately 700 workers, continuing a trend of recent job cuts in the tech industry at the beginning of 2024. summary: Pinterest CEO Bill Ready argues that the social media industry must learn from the mistakes of "Big Tobacco" and take responsibility for the harms it causes, particularly to young people. He advocates for using AI to promote positive content, improve youth online safety, and implement special protections for teens, citing Pinterest's efforts to retrain its AI for inspiring content and restrict teen accounts. Ready stresses that a business model focused on positivity is achievable and necessary to avoid social media becoming the next "Big Tobacco."

title: GNU C Library vulnerabilities could impact Linux systems, security company says
summary: Security company Qualys has identified several "significant" vulnerabilities in the GNU C Library (glibc), a fundamental component of Linux systems. These flaws, including a critical heap-based buffer overflow (CVE-2023-6246) that could allow local privilege escalation to root access, affect major Linux distributions like Debian, Ubuntu, and Fedora. summary: During a tense Senate hearing on child safety, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg offered an unscripted apology to families of children who were victims of sexual exploitation on social media platforms. summary: EA SPORTS Madden NFL 24 has predicted the Kansas City Chiefs to defeat the San Francisco 49ers 30-28 in Super Bowl LVIII, with Patrick Mahomes earning his second consecutive Super Bowl MVP.
